name: slice
signature:
slice(X, Y, Z, V, xslice, yslice, zslice)
slice(V, xslice, yslice, zslice)
slice(X, Y, Z, V, Xi, Yi, Zi)
slice(___, method)
h = slice(___)
summary: Draws planes through a 3-D volume, colored by the volume's values.
doc: Each value of xslice is the plane x = xslice(k), and likewise for yslice and zslice ([] for none); the surfaces come in that order, x-planes first. Each plane is a surface on the volume's grid lines, colored by V interpolated there as interp3 does it (method 'linear', the default, 'nearest', 'cubic' or 'spline'); a plane outside the volume is all NaN. Matrices Xi, Yi and Zi of one size give one surface through those points instead. shading interp and colorbar make the planes easier to read.

name: isosurface
signature:
fv = isosurface(X, Y, Z, V, isovalue)
fv = isosurface(V, isovalue)
fvc = isosurface(___, colors)
[f, v] = isosurface(___)
[f, v, c] = isosurface(___)
isosurface(___)
isosurface(___, 'noshare')
summary: The surface where a 3-D volume takes a given value, as faces and vertices for patch.
doc: Marching cubes on V's grid: each vertex lies on a grid edge where V crosses isovalue, linearly between the edge's two values; faces are triangles (an F-by-3 array of indices into the N-by-3 vertices), wound so that their normals point toward higher values. Vertices are shared between faces, and a face whose corners meet at one point (where V equals isovalue at a grid point) is left out; with 'noshare', each face has its own three vertices and none is left out. Without X, Y and Z the vertices are in index units (x the column). colors, an array of V's size, is interpolated at the vertices (facevertexcdata). A face with a corner on a grid edge to a NaN in V is left out. With no output, the surface is drawn as a patch in the current axes. Pass the result to patch, then camlight and lighting gouraud to see its shape.
differs: The isovalue is required: MATLAB picks one when it is left out, by a rule it does not document.

Faces are not in MATLAB's order, and where a cell's polygon can be cut into triangles along other diagonals the cut is Sagebrush's own: the vertices, counts and topology are MATLAB's, but area and volume can differ slightly where cells are ambiguous.
An Inf or -Inf in V is treated as a NaN (the faces with a corner on an edge to it are left out), where MATLAB gives NaN vertices.

name: isonormals
signature:
n = isonormals(X, Y, Z, V, vertices)
n = isonormals(V, vertices)
isonormals(___, p)
isonormals(___, 'negate')
summary: Normals at an isosurface's vertices, from the volume's gradient, for smooth lighting.
doc: The gradient of V (central differences, one-sided at the ends, as gradient computes it), interpolated linearly at each vertex and made unit length; 'negate' reverses them. Given the patch p instead of vertices, sets p.VertexNormals.
differs: The normals point along V's gradient, toward higher values; that this is MATLAB's sign has not been checked against MATLAB yet.
